newsitem.title: BULGARIA: Bulgaria lev closes firmer to mark, softer vs dlr.
newsitem.headline: Bulgaria lev closes firmer to mark, softer vs dlr.

text.p: The Bulgarian lev closed around 994-995 per mark, slightly firmer than the opening 994-996 due to high foreign currency supply ahead of the planned lev peg under a currency board, dealers said.
* The lev is to be pegged at 1,000 per mark under a currency board mechanism to be launched on Tuesday.

* The Bulgarian National Bank (BNB) was seen buying marks at 995 levs. The central bank governor said last week the BNB would buy the mark at 995 levs and sell it at 1,000 under the currency board system.
* Commercial banks bought the mark from other banks and clients at rates a touch lower that the BNB's 995 levs so that they could then sell the foreign currency to the central bank, dealers said.
* Banks were offering foreign currency for levs to invest in government securities, in the absence of investment alternatives after the central bank stopped its open market operations.
* The Finance Ministry offered on Monday three discount T-bill issues with a total par value of 105 billion levs and maturities of three, six and 12 months.

* Foreign currency demand was low as in the previous days it was mainly bought for piling up of forex positions ahead of the currency board, because foreign currency investment were seen as higher-yielding than lev-denominated instruments.
* The lev closed at 1,733-1,738 per dollar against the morning's 1,725-1,730, following the domestic lev/mark rate and the mark/dollar cross on international markets.
